items.followUp: Define apiculture and name one product obtained from it.

rubric.description: Identifies horticulture as the cultivation of garden plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the cultivation of garden plants, including fruits, vegetables or ornamental plants.

rubric.why: Identifies horticulture as a field of study or practice.
rubric.description: States that horticulture is a branch of agriculture or applied biology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a branch of agriculture or applied biology.

modelAnswer: Horticulture is the branch of agriculture concerned with the cultivation of garden plants, including fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants.

items.followUp: What are the major bioelements found in living organisms?

rubric.why: Defines bioelements in relation to living things.
rubric.description: Defines bioelements as chemical elements present in or necessary for living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.
Award 1 mark for at least two correct examples, such as carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen.

modelAnswer: Bioelements are the chemical elements present in living organisms and needed for life.
Examples include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen.

items.followUp: Give two examples of unicellular organisms other than Amoeba.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

rubric.why: Requires a second valid example as asked.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct example; do not award the second mark for a repeated example.

modelAnswer: Examples of unicellular organisms are Amoeba and bacteria.

items.followUp: Define pathogen and give one example.

rubric.why: Identifies the interval that defines the incubation period.
rubric.description: States that it is the time between infection or entry of a pathogen and the appearance of symptoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct interval.

rubric.why: Includes the endpoint of the period.
rubric.description: Specifies that the period ends when symptoms appear.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the definition clearly includes the appearance of symptoms.

modelAnswer: The incubation period is the time between the entry of a pathogen into the body and the appearance of disease symptoms.

items.followUp: Define a scientific theory and give one biological example.

rubric.why: Tests the meaning of a scientific law or principle.
rubric.description: Defines a law or principle as a generalization supported by repeated observations or experiments and accepted generally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition conveying this idea.

rubric.why: Requires examples of biological laws or principles.
rubric.description: Gives two valid examples of biological laws or principles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two valid examples; accept Mendel's laws, such as the law of inheritance or law of dominance.

modelAnswer: A law or principle is a general statement based on repeated observations or experiments and accepted as generally true.
Examples include Mendel's laws of inheritance, such as the law of dominance and the law of segregation.

items.followUp: State two functions of stomata in leaves.

rubric.why: Identifies one function of the epidermal tissue.
rubric.description: Gives one valid function, such as protection, reducing water loss, gas exchange or absorption by root epidermis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct function.

rubric.description: Gives a second valid function of epidermal tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct correct function.

modelAnswer: Epidermal tissues protect the plant from injury and infection.
They reduce water loss; in roots, epidermal cells also absorb water and minerals, while stomata allow gas exchange.

items.followUp: What is meant by a vulnerable species?

rubric.why: Distinguishes extinction as the complete disappearance of a species.
rubric.description: Defines an extinct species as one with no living members remaining.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition conveying complete disappearance.

rubric.why: Identifies the risk faced by endangered species.
rubric.description: Defines an endangered species as one at risk of extinction, often because its population is small or declining.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

modelAnswer: An extinct species has no living members remaining.
An endangered species is one whose population is so small or declining that it is at risk of extinction.

items.followUp: Name two measures that individuals can take to help conserve biodiversity.

rubric.why: Includes protection of species in their natural habitats.
rubric.description: Mentions establishing or maintaining protected areas or protecting habitats.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one appropriate in-situ conservation measure.

rubric.description: Mentions a further strategy, such as sustainable use, enforcing wildlife laws, public awareness or ex-situ conservation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one appropriate additional measure.

modelAnswer: Pakistan's National Conservation Strategy aims to conserve biodiversity by protecting habitats through national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and game reserves.
It also supports sustainable use of biological resources and conservation measures such as enforcing wildlife laws and raising public awareness.
